strategy.summary: Reproduce the pandas scalar Timedelta integer-division precision bug (GH#66551 integer-divisor half) by building pandas at the buggy commit 12d8a044697f and running the developer's test_td_div_integer_exact; it should fail on buggy (float64 quotient rounding, NaT/OverflowError at Timedelta.min/max, wrong low digit at 36028797018963967/2) and pass on the fixed revision with exact truncating int division.

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy, python-dateutil, tzdata and Cython have no documented constraint and no era ceiling in the evidence; versions are chosen by the strategy (latest compatible with the buggy commit's build) and not pinned from evidence
Python version is not stated by the evidence, so it is left null and should be the interpreter the buggy commit supports

strategy.reproducing_test: pandas/tests/scalar/timedelta/test_arithmetic.py::TestTimedeltaMultiplicationDivision::test_td_div_integer_exact (parametrized over Timedelta.min/max with divisor 1 and -1, 2**53+1 with divisor 1, and 36028797018963967 with divisors 2 and -2)
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 12d8a044697f the test fails: Timedelta.min/1 yields NaT or the assertion fails, Timedelta.max/1 raises OverflowError, and 36028797018963967/2 gives ...984 instead of ...983 because the quotient is computed in float64. On the fixed revision the same test passes: scalar and pd.array-based division both return exact truncated int64 results equal to the expected values.
strategy.numerical_probe: Timedelta(36028797018963967, unit='ns') / 2 compared with 18014398509481983 at the _value level

input_output_examples.buggy_output: NaT (per commit message) or AssertionError (per PR reproducer)
OverflowError: Python int too large to convert to C long

risks: The Python version and NumPy version are not stated; the failure depends on float64 division of int64 values, which is platform-independent in IEEE double arithmetic, but the buggy commit must build cleanly on the chosen interpreter.
Only the integer-divisor half of GH#66551 is fixed; float divisors are out of scope and must not be used in reproduction.

The PR reproducer outputs are inconsistent (AssertionError vs OverflowError vs NaT vs wrong digit); the developer test is the authority for the transition, and a mismatch in exact observed message does not change the pass/fail transition.

The test's second assertion uses pd.array([td]) / divisor, which exercises the vectorized path; if that path also differs at the buggy commit the failure may come from there rather than the scalar path, so the first assertion is the one to read.
Test uses Timedelta.min._value and Timedelta.max._value at collection time; if pandas fails to import on the buggy build, collection errors will mask the transition.
No sanitiser or special architecture is evidenced; the bug should reproduce on any x86_64 or arm64 Linux build, but this is not confirmed by the evidence.

oracle.reference_source: numpy int64 floor/truncation semantics and the vectorized pd.array path, as stated in the PR and test comment
oracle.why: The test asserts exact int64 _value equality, so no tolerance applies.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On the buggy revision the scalar division computes <int64_t>(self._value / other) in float64; for Timedelta.min the rounded quotient misbehaves (NaT or assertion failure), Timedelta.max raises OverflowError, and 36028797018963967/2 yields ...984 instead of ...983, so result._value == expected is False or an exception is raised.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the quotient is computed exactly with Python ints and truncated toward zero, so result._value equals the expected value for all parametrized cases and the vectorized comparison also matches.
